report.summary: Critical off-by-one in window_runs causes missing last window when file has exactly run_len lines. Error-handling silently degrades fingerprints on tokenizer errors and unterminated block comments. No concurrency/filesystem issues. The docstring for window_runs claims full window coverage but implementation misses the boundary case.
risks: False negatives in window clone detection: files with exactly run_len significant lines produce no run hashes.
Silent fingerprint degradation on Python tokenizer errors may cause clone drift.
Unterminated block comments silently truncate source, risking fabricated clones.
todos: Fix off-by-one in window_runs: use range(max(0, len(norm) - run_len + 1)).
Log a warning when Python normalization falls back to regex.
Consider raising an error or logging when _strip_comments_generic encounters an unterminated block comment.

handoff.suggestion: In window_runs, change 'range(max(0, len(norm) - run_len))' to 'range(max(0, len(norm) - run_len + 1))' to include the last possible window. For Python normalization fallback, emit a warning via logging or return a sentinel. For unterminated block comments in _strip_comments_generic, if no close_ found, consider logging and optionally preserving the rest of the source after a reasonable limit.
